title: Residual-certified mass through preparation and clean projection
question:
Let \(n\ge 0\) and let \(r_0,\ldots,r_n\) be finite nonnegative bond dimensions with \(r_0=r_n=1\). For \(j=1,\ldots,n\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(A_j^t\) be a real \(r_{j-1}\)-by-\(r_j\) matrix. The raw vector \(x\in\mathbb R^{2^n}\) has coordinates
\[
x_s=(A_1^{s_1}\cdots A_n^{s_n})_{1,1},
\]
with one empty word and empty product \(I_1\) when \(n=0\). Use Euclidean vector norms and their induced operator norms. Write
\[
T_j(Z)=\sum_{t=0}^1 A_j^t Z(A_j^t)^{\mathsf T},\qquad
E_n=I_1,\qquad E_{j-1}=T_j(E_j).
\]
You may use the exact Gram identity \(E_0(1,1)=\lVert x\rVert^2\).

Suppose supplied real matrices \(\widehat E_j\) of size \(r_j\)-by-\(r_j\) satisfy \(\widehat E_n=I_1\), and supplied nonnegative certificates \(\varepsilon_j,L_j\) obey
\[
\lVert\widehat E_{j-1}-T_j(\widehat E_j)\rVert\le\varepsilon_j,
\qquad \sum_t\lVert A_j^t\rVert^2\le L_j.
\]
No positivity or canonicality of the \(\widehat E_j\) or the cores is assumed. Derive an explicit a posteriori number \(\beta\), in terms of the \(\varepsilon_j,L_j\), with
\[
\bigl|\widehat E_0(1,1)-\lVert x\rVert^2\bigr|\le\beta.
\]
Give the \(n=0\) convention. Explain why propagation factors from preceding cores cannot in general be omitted; exhibit a scalar-bond example in which replacing \(\beta\) by \(\sum_j\varepsilon_j\) would falsely certify positive mass for the zero raw vector.

For the remainder use your certified \(m:=\widehat E_0(1,1)-\beta\) and assume \(m>0\). A second raw vector \(y\in\mathbb R^{2^n}\) satisfies \(\lVert x-y\rVert\le\delta\), where \(0\le\delta<\sqrt m\). Prove \(x\) and \(y\) nonzero before defining \(\psi=x/\lVert x\rVert\) and \(\phi=y/\lVert y\rVert\). You may use the supplied normalization inequality
\[
\left\lVert\frac{u}{\lVert u\rVert}-\frac{v}{\lVert v\rVert}\right\rVert
\le\frac{2\lVert u-v\rVert}{\lVert u\rVert}
\]
for nonzero finite real or complex vectors \(u,v\).

Let \(H=\mathbb C^{2^n}\), \(K=\mathbb C^{2^a}\) with \(a\ge0\), \(Jv=|0^a\rangle\otimes v\), and \(P=JJ^\dagger\), in the fixed order \(K\otimes H\). All workspace is included in \(K\). Two actual unitary gate lists \(U\) and \(V\) have the same length, instruction types and physical targets in every position; only Y-rotation angles differ. A rotation is
\[
R(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\theta/2)&-\sin(\theta/2)\\ \sin(\theta/2)&\cos(\theta/2)\end{pmatrix},
\]
and the supplied angle error at rotation occurrence \(k\) is \(d_k\ge0\). All other gates agree exactly, including phases. Chronological products place the first gate rightmost. You may use the supplied aligned-circuit bound
\[
\lVert V-U\rVert\le\gamma:=\frac12\sum_k d_k.
\]
The exact preparation action is \(U|0^{a+n}\rangle=J\phi\).

For \(\Omega=V|0^{a+n}\rangle\) and \(\tau:=2\delta/\sqrt m+\gamma\), derive a full-output bound relative to \(J\psi\). Assume \(\tau<1\) before conditioning. Decompose \(\Omega\) into clean and rejected branches, prove the clean branch is nonzero, and prove that its success probability \(p\) and normalized accepted system vector \(\psi_{\mathrm{acc}}\) satisfy
\[
p\ge(1-\tau^2/2)^2,\qquad
\lVert\psi_{\mathrm{acc}}-\psi\rVert\le\tau.
\]
In particular justify the conditional-vector bound from the unit norm of the full output; do not silently replace it by a phase-minimized distance. Explain why \(\tau<1\) is a sufficient rather than a claimed sharp threshold, and give a unitary example with zero clean success and full-output distance \(\sqrt2\) from a clean target.

Check zero residuals, zero data/gate errors, \(n=0\), \(a=0\), and an internal zero bond dimension. Keep cases that contradict \(m>0\) separate from the active normalization theorem. State exactly which conclusions depend on the certified residuals, raw-data error, and actual circuit action/alignment; no floating-point residual certifier, angle supplier, state-loading algorithm, finite-gate-set compiler, or runtime bound is supplied.
assumptions: Finite real scalar-boundary tensor train with fixed bit order; approximate Gram environments have exact terminal I_1 and certified local operator-norm residuals ε_j and transfer bounds L_j.
For the normalization/circuit branch only: m=Ē_0(1,1)−β>0 and ||x−y||≤δ<√m with δ≥0.
The actual unitary lists are positionally aligned, differing only in same-target half-angle Y rotations with certified errors d_k; all other instructions and exact phases agree.
After φ is proved well-defined, the exact list has complete output U|0^{a+n}⟩=Jφ, including clean workspace; τ=2δ/√m+γ<1 is imposed before conditional normalization.
Exact Gram, normalization stability and aligned-circuit norm bounds are supplied interfaces; residual propagation, margin checks and downstream projection estimates are to be derived.
conventions: All vector distances compare exact representatives. Complex inner products are conjugate-linear in the first argument; real vectors embed componentwise in H.
Registers are ordered ancilla/workspace K then system H; J is the clean isometry and success projects every qubit of K onto zero.
Empty products equal 1 and empty sums 0; a zero-qubit system is one-dimensional. Zero-dimensional internal bonds are allowed and force the raw contraction to vanish.
The false-certificate example and vanishing-mass cases are diagnostics outside the active m>0 branch. No normalization of a zero vector is defined.

title: Two-sided LCU from approximate clean columns
question:
Let \(K=\mathbb C^r\) with \(r\ge1\) and distinguished basis vector \(|0\rangle\), and let \(H=\mathbb C^d\) with \(d\ge1\). Fix the order \(K\otimes H\). For \(j=1,\ldots,r\) let \(U_j:H\to H\) be unitary and \(c_j\in\mathbb C\), not all zero. Put
\[
\alpha=\sum_j|c_j|>0,\qquad A=\sum_j c_jU_j,
\]
\[
\omega_j=\begin{cases}c_j/|c_j|,&c_j\ne0,\\1,&c_j=0,\end{cases}
\qquad l_j=\sqrt{|c_j|/\alpha},\qquad r_j=\omega_j\sqrt{|c_j|/\alpha}.
\]
Here the symbol \(r_j\) is a vector coordinate, while \(r\) is the selector dimension. Let
\[
S=\sum_j|j\rangle\langle j|\otimes U_j.
\]

Available unitaries \(Q_L,Q_R\) on \(K\) have clean columns \(\widetilde l=Q_L|0\rangle\) and \(\widetilde r=Q_R|0\rangle\) satisfying the exact-representative bounds
\[
\lVert\widetilde l-l\rVert\le\delta_L,\qquad
\lVert\widetilde r-r\rVert\le\delta_R,
\qquad\delta_L,\delta_R\ge0.
\]
An available unitary \(\widetilde S\) on \(K\otimes H\) satisfies \(\lVert\widetilde S-S\rVert\le\eta\), \(\eta\ge0\), in induced Euclidean operator norm; \(\widetilde S\) need not preserve the selector. The specified composite uses the actual adjoint \(Q_L^\dagger\) exactly:
\[
\widetilde W=(Q_L^\dagger\otimes I)\widetilde S(Q_R\otimes I),\qquad
Jv=|0\rangle\otimes v,\qquad
\widetilde B=J^\dagger\widetilde WJ.
\]
All work of this mathematical interface is in \(K\otimes H\).

Derive the clean-column sandwich formula for \(\widetilde B\). Prove the exact target formula
\[
(\langle l|\otimes I)S(|r\rangle\otimes I)=A/\alpha
\]
and derive the approximate block-encoding guarantee
\[
\lVert A-\alpha\widetilde B\rVert\le\alpha\min\{2,\delta_L+\delta_R+\eta\}.
\]
Your proof must explain why no operator-norm approximation of \(Q_L\) or \(Q_R\) to a chosen full PREPARE unitary is required, and must justify unitarity and contraction facts used in the estimate. For ideal \(S\) in the middle, explicitly compute the implemented coefficients \(\overline{\widetilde l_j}\,\widetilde r_j\) and prove their \(\ell^1\) deviation from \(c_j/\alpha\) is at most \(\delta_L+\delta_R\). Explain whether this coefficient route and the direct sandwich-norm route are alternative proofs or jointly necessary assumptions.

Suppose instead that one only knows
\[
\lVert\widetilde l-e^{i\theta_L}l\rVert\le\delta_L,\qquad
\lVert\widetilde r-e^{i\theta_R}r\rVert\le\delta_R
\]
for real phases \(\theta_L,\theta_R\). Derive the corresponding phase-shifted target and an explicit bound on \(\lVert A-\alpha\widetilde B\rVert\) that includes the phase mismatch. Give a concrete unitary example with perfect separate state fidelities but wrong exact block, and state a sufficient phase relation that restores the previous guarantee. The question concerns exact block representatives, even if an isolated prepared state is physically unchanged by its global phase.

Prove that changing the off-clean columns of \(Q_L\) or \(Q_R\) while retaining unitarity and their clean columns cannot change \(\widetilde B\) for fixed \(\widetilde S\); give an explicit pair of unitary completions at operator distance \(2\) with the same clean column. Discuss zero coefficients, \(r=1\), \(\delta_L=\delta_R=\eta=0\), and the excluded all-zero coefficient case. Explain why the mathematical availability of prepared state vectors alone does not supply an executable adjoint, coherent SELECT, clean-work implementation or finite-bit resource guarantee. A successful clean projection need not occur deterministically.
assumptions: Finite complex selector and system spaces of dimensions r≥1 and d≥1, with a fixed distinguished clean selector basis vector and tensor order K⊗H.
Every U_j is unitary; coefficients c_j are not all zero so α=Σ_j|c_j|>0.
Q_L,Q_R,S̃ are actual unitaries and the specified composite uses the actual Q_L†; clean-column errors and SELECT error are certified in Euclidean/induced operator norms.
The principal branch compares exact clean-column representatives. The later phase branch replaces those estimates by phase-referenced estimates with real θ_L,θ_R.
conventions: Complex inner products are conjugate-linear in the first argument; a bra ⟨l| therefore has coefficients conj(l_j).
Matrix products act on column vectors from the rightmost factor first. No transpose replaces the complex adjoint.
The clean block projects the selector at both ends; a nonclean rejected sector may remain in the full output.
The coefficient ℓ¹ route and direct sandwich route may be used as alternative sufficient derivations; neither is an extra hypothesis on the inputs.
No approximate inverse is substituted for Q_L†. State-generation access alone is weaker than the available-unitary interface assumed in the main branch.

title: Finite-grid Gram contraction: roundoff, range and a certified normalizer
question:
Work over the real numbers. Let \(n\ge0\), let \(d_0=d_n=1\) and \(d_j\ge1\), and let the two slices \(A_j^0,A_j^1\in\mathbb R^{d_{j-1}\times d_j}\) of core \(j\) be supplied dyadic rationals. Their denominators divide \(2^{b_{\rm in}}\), and every entry has magnitude at most a supplied \(M_j\ge0\). For an ordered bit word \(s\in\{0,1\}^n\), put \(x_s=A_1^{s_1}\cdots A_n^{s_n}\), a scalar. An empty product is 1 and there is one empty word. You may use, without re-proving, the exact Gram identity
\[
E_n=[1],\qquad E_{j-1}=\sum_{t=0}^1 A_j^t E_j(A_j^t)^T,
\qquad (E_0)_{11}=\sum_s x_s^2=\|x\|_2^2.
\]

Here is a particular finite-grid algorithm, not a floating-point black box. Choose an integer \(b\ge b_{\rm in}\), use the grid \(h\mathbb Z\) with \(h=2^{-b}\), and let \(Q_b\) round to a nearest grid point with any fixed tie convention; hence \(|Q_b(z)-z|\le u=h/2\). Inputs, 0 and 1 are represented exactly. Set \(\widehat E_n=[1]\). At step \(j\), with \(m=d_j\), compute, separately for each \(t\), \(\widehat T^t\) by multiplying \(A_j^t\widehat E_j\) with the following dot-product schedule: start the accumulator at 0, round each scalar product with \(Q_b\), then round every addition into the accumulator. In the same way compute \(\widehat S^t\) from \(\widehat T^t(A_j^t)^T\), and set each entry of \(\widehat E_{j-1}\) to \(Q_b(\widehat S^0+\widehat S^1)\). Do not impose symmetry or positivity on the rounded environment. Initially reason on the unbounded grid; a finite signed range will be chosen from your intermediate-value bounds.

1. With \(\|F\|_{\max}=\max_{a,c}|F_{ac}|\), derive a uniform error certificate for this schedule. In particular, prove that the safe constants
\[
L_j=2d_j^2M_j^2,\qquad R_j=4d_j^2M_j+4d_j+1
\]
permit \(e_n=0\) and \(e_{j-1}\le L_j e_j+uR_j\), where \(e_j=\|\widehat E_j-E_j\|_{\max}\). Derive an explicit unrolled bound \(e_0\le uC_0\), and specify a backwards recurrence for all \(C_j\). Tighter constants from exact grid additions are also acceptable if every later bound is updated consistently. Bound the magnitudes of stored environments, both kinds of scalar products and all partial sums, and explain how finitely many integer bits can be chosen to prevent overflow. A range bound for only the final scalar is insufficient.

2. Let an independent certificate supply \(\|x\|_2\ge\mu>0\). When the rounded scalar \(\widehat s=(\widehat E_0)_{11}\) is positive, take one correctly rounded square root \(\widehat r=Q_b(\sqrt{\widehat s})\). Derive explicit sufficient conditions for \(\widehat s>0\) and \(\widehat r>0\), and a quantitative bound on
\[
\left\|\frac{x}{\widehat r}-\frac{x}{\|x\|_2}\right\|_2.
\]
The numerator \(x\) and the displayed divisions are exact mathematical quantities here; output-coordinate rounding and a circuit implementation are not included. For any requested \(\varepsilon>0\), give a sufficient inequality on \(u\), and therefore an integer choice of \(b\ge b_{\rm in}\), that establishes both positivity facts and error at most \(\varepsilon\), without first assuming those positivity facts. State why \(x/\widehat r\) need not have norm exactly one.

3. Check \(n=0\), zero cores and zero mass with correctly scoped premises. For any fixed \(b\ge2\), give a legal one-core grid input with nonzero exact mass whose computed \(\widehat s\) is zero. Explain what this says about a guarantee without a lower-mass/precision margin, and why the exact-real Gram identity or an exact-real operation count alone is not the finite-grid certificate proved here. No claim about optimal constants, bit-operation runtime, core-generation error or quantum gate synthesis is requested.
assumptions: Finite real scalar-boundary train with strictly positive bond dimensions and exact supplied dyadic core entries.
A known finite magnitude bound M_j for each core and an integer input precision b_in; working b is at least b_in.
The precise Q_b multiplication/addition schedule in the question; nearest-grid rounding has absolute error at most u=2^(-b-1).
The normalization branch separately receives an independent true-norm lower bound mu>0; the raw-error branch does not assume positive mass.
The correctly rounded square root is invoked only after positivity of its input has been established.
conventions: Core products are ordered left-to-right by emitted bit; real transpose, entrywise maximum matrix norm and Euclidean vector norm are distinct.
There is one empty word; an empty product is one. All environment matrices have positive dimensions.
Q_b has a fixed tie rule; all stored grid additions are actually exact on an unbounded grid, but charging u for them yields the requested conservative certificate.
x/r_hat is an exactly divided mathematical vector; no output amplitude rounding, input-core generation error, circuit or bit-runtime claim is included.

title: Sequential approximate isometries: multiplicative mass and target-error growth
question:
Let \(n\ge0\) and let \(H_j=\mathbb C^{d_j}\) with finite \(d_j\ge1\). Core \(j\) is a linear map
\[
V_j:H_{j-1}\longrightarrow\mathbb C^2\otimes H_j\qquad(1\le j\le n).
\]
All spaces carry their standard Euclidean inner products; \(\dagger\) means conjugate transpose and \(\|\cdot\|_{\rm op}\) is the induced operator norm. Rows label outputs and columns label inputs. A new bit is appended after all previously emitted bits, and the bond remains the final tensor factor. Put \(T_0=I_{H_0}\) and, using only the corresponding norm-preserving regrouping,
\[
T_j=(I_{(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes(j-1)}}\otimes V_j)T_{j-1}.
\]
Assume the local Gram defects satisfy
\[
\|V_j^\dagger V_j-I_{H_{j-1}}\|_{\rm op}\le\eta_j,
\qquad 0\le\eta_j<1.
\]
These are approximate linear maps; neither full unitary completions nor a physical channel realization is assumed.

1. Prove a one-step norm-squared inequality valid for every vector on passive emitted bits and the incoming bond, including vectors entangled between those factors. Use it to derive, for every \(v\in H_0\) and every length \(n\),
\[
\prod_{j=1}^n(1-\eta_j)\|v\|_2^2
\le\|T_n v\|_2^2\le
\prod_{j=1}^n(1+\eta_j)\|v\|_2^2.
\]
Give the resulting bound on \(\|T_n^\dagger T_n-I\|_{\rm op}\). Show that the two mass endpoints can each be attained by legal bond-dimension-one trains. Do not replace the product by \(1\pm\sum_j\eta_j\) as an exact general inequality without justification.

2. Does zero defect at every stage imply fidelity to a specified target train? Give two legal one-stage, bond-dimension-one trains with zero defects whose outputs from initial scalar 1 are orthogonal. State exactly what Gram/mass control therefore certifies and what target information it lacks.

3. In this separate comparison branch, suppose additional maps \(W_j:H_{j-1}\to\mathbb C^2\otimes H_j\) are exact isometries, \(W_j^\dagger W_j=I\), and \(\|V_j-W_j\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_j\) with \(\epsilon_j\ge0\). Let \(S_n\) be their sequential composition in the same order as \(T_n\). For a unit vector \(v\), prove the growth-weighted target bound
\[
\|T_n v-S_n v\|_2
\le\sum_{k=1}^n\epsilon_k\prod_{j=k+1}^n\sqrt{1+\eta_j}.
\]
Explain why the product weights involve stages later than the inserted discrepancy. Give a two-stage, bond-dimension-one example satisfying all stated premises for which the simpler claim \(\|T_2v-S_2v\|_2\le\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2\) fails. This is an unnormalized vector bound; no normalization or postselection is implicit.

4. Check the empty chain, zero input, and the exact-isometry specialization. Separately replace the strict local condition by \(\eta_j=1\) and show why a positive lower mass is then not guaranteed. Explain why these conclusions alone give neither a unitary-circuit synthesis theorem nor terminal-bond cleanup. Each diagnostic must state which premises it retains or replaces.
assumptions: Finite nonzero complex bond spaces with standard Euclidean inner products and dimension-compatible core maps.
For the main mass branch, each local operator Gram defect is bounded by 0<=eta_j<1.
Only the comparison branch receives exact ideal isometries W_j and operator differences bounded by epsilon_j; unit input is required only for its displayed absolute error budget.
The eta_j=1 diagnostic replaces the strict defect premise; the zero-input diagnostic does not retain the comparison branch unit-input premise.
conventions: Each core maps an incoming column vector to a new-bit and outgoing-bond column vector; emitted bits are ordered chronologically and the bond is last.
Adjoint is conjugate transpose; all norms are induced Euclidean norms and the tensor regrouping is norm-preserving.
Gram control concerns unnormalized linear maps; it does not by itself define a physical probability-preserving channel or clean terminal register.
All empty products equal one and empty sums equal zero.

title: A reversible finite-bit phase supplier with a reusable gradient catalyst
question:
Let \(m\geq1\), \(M=2^m\), and let \(X\) be an \(n\)-qubit input register. Integer registers use little-endian bits: \(z=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}2^jz_j\). An explicitly supplied reversible circuit \(B\), built from \(X\), CNOT and Toffoli gates, acts on \((X,Q,W)\), where \(Q\) has \(m\) bits and \(W\) has \(w\) bits. Its clean-input action is
\[
B|x,0^m,0^w\rangle=|x,q_x,\gamma_x\rangle,
\qquad q_x\in\{0,\ldots,M-1\}.
\]
The entire gate list is supplied, with gate-count vector \(g_B=(b_X,b_{\mathrm{CX}},b_{\mathrm{CCX}})\); neither \(\gamma_x=0\) nor a cost bound polynomial in \(n,m\) is promised. All supplier work is included in \(W\). Define
\[
|G_m\rangle=M^{-1/2}\sum_{y=0}^{M-1}e^{2\pi i y/M}|y\rangle,
\qquad D_q|x\rangle=e^{-2\pi i q_x/M}|x\rangle.
\]
Use a separate \(m\)-qubit register \(Y\) for this phase-gradient state and clean scratch \(A\). The permitted logical gate set additionally contains Hadamard \(H\) and the exactly specified phase gates \(P(\theta)=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\theta})\) at dyadic multiples of \(\pi\); this is an ideal logical model, not an assumed fixed-finite-gate compilation.

Construct a coherent implementation of \(D_q\) from \(B\), modular addition \(|q,y\rangle\mapsto|q,y+q\bmod M\rangle\), and an actual inverse of \(B\). Prove the full register action, including arbitrary superpositions of \(x\), the sign of the phase despite modular wrapping, restoration of both \(Q,W\), and return of \(Y\) as a separable reusable \(|G_m\rangle\). Explain precisely why tracing the supplier record is not the advertised clean implementation.

The modular adder itself must be supplied, not treated as a unit-cost oracle. Use this explicit route: for each \(j=0,\ldots,m-1\), conditionally increment the suffix \(Y_j,\ldots,Y_{m-1}\) when \(Q_j=1\); within an increment visit target bits from highest to lowest. Derive each controlled flip from the binary carry rule. Implement a NOT with \(k\geq2\) distinct controls by computing their conjunction along a clean chain, flipping the target, and reversing the chain; a one-control NOT is CNOT. Derive a closed expression for the resulting Toffoli count, the CNOT count, and the maximum simultaneously needed clean scratch. Prove that all scratch is restored and the arithmetic is correct for every word, rather than giving only a small-width example.

Construct a product-gate preparation \(F_m|0^m\rangle=|G_m\rangle\). For \(L\geq1\) uses with the same supplied \(B\), give the complete gate-count and live-qubit ledger both when the catalyst is returned for reuse and when it is finally reset coherently by \(F_m^\dagger\). Charge the supplied computation and its inverse on every use; distinguish these costs from the one-time catalyst preparation. Do not assume any of these registers can be erased or inverses obtained from mere forward black-box access.

As a stability test, replace \(F_m\) by an actual unitary preparation \(\widetilde F_m\) whose prepared vector has Euclidean error at most \(\eta\). Keep every supplier and adder exact, permit arbitrary interleaved unitaries acting only on the data registers, and reuse the same catalyst for \(L\) coherent uses. Bound the full output error relative to the ideal data output tensored with \(|G_m\rangle\), and separately bound the full clean-zero output error after applying the actual \(\widetilde F_m^\dagger\). Determine whether an unavoidable factor \(L\) follows from catalyst preparation error alone, and whether exact catalyst factorization still follows. Keep Euclidean vector error, clean-zero return, and a gate-synthesis guarantee distinct; treat \(m=1\) and the optional zero-bit extension explicitly.
assumptions: The complete reversible supplier gate list B and its exact clean-input action are given; its data-dependent garbage is explicitly retained in W.
The modular-adder circuit and catalyst preparation are to be constructed in the stated logical gate model.
The approximate-catalyst subproblem assumes an actual unitary preparation and its actual inverse; all intervening suppliers/adders are exact.
conventions: Register order is X,Q,W,Y,A, with little-endian integer words; the adder overwrites Y and preserves Q.
The gradient has positive Fourier exponent, so addition kicks back a negative phase.
Logical gate counts and finite-word storage are distinguished from fixed-finite-gate synthesis, connectivity, depth and supplier construction costs.

title: Sharp coherent error from approximate basis-column guarantees
question:
Let \(N\geq1\), let \(\mathcal H\) be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, and let \(U,V:\mathbb C^N\to\mathcal H\) be isometries: \(U^\dagger U=V^\dagger V=I_N\). Their columns include the complete output, including all work registers; no measurement, postselection, or trace-out occurs. Let \(e_0,\ldots,e_{N-1}\) be the standard input basis and suppose exact representative-wise guarantees
\[
\|(V-U)e_j\|_2\leq\varepsilon_j,\qquad \varepsilon_j\geq0,
\]
are known separately for every basis input. All operator norms below are induced Euclidean norms; no minimization over global phase is built into this promise.

Put \(E=V-U\) and \(G_{jk}=\langle Ee_j,Ee_k\rangle\), using an inner product conjugate-linear in its first argument. Derive the exact quadratic form for the error on an arbitrary coherent unit input and the resulting characterization of \(\|E\|\) in terms of \(G\). Decide whether the column guarantees alone imply the dimension-free bound \(\|E\|\leq\max_j\varepsilon_j\). Find the sharp universal bound obtainable from the whole vector \((\varepsilon_j)_j\), including the isometry cap, and prove sharpness for EVERY choice of these nonnegative tolerances by constructing square unitaries on \(\mathbb C^N\). An arbitrary unconstrained error matrix is not a sufficient sharpness witness. Derive the uniform-tolerance corollary and identify when the cap takes over.

For \(N\geq2\), give an explicit family of unitaries whose error on every computational-basis input tends to zero as \(N\) grows while their operator distance stays maximal. A saturating input that changes only by an overall sign does not by itself demonstrate operational distinguishability: also give a normalized superposition on which the intended and actual output states are orthogonal, with a specified distinguishing measurement. Report both the Euclidean vector distance and the trace distance \(\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1\) for this latter input, and explain why the first saturating input has different physical-state behavior.

Finally state what additional error-geometry condition WOULD yield a dimension-free bound from the same column norms, and justify it using \(G\). Explain briefly why an explicitly retained orthogonal branch label can supply that condition for controlled branch outputs, whereas linearity by itself does not. This comparison is only a boundary explanation, not a request to re-prove general controlled-family phase correction. Cover zero tolerances, \(N=1\), and exact column agreement. Do not replace full-output Euclidean promises by per-input probability agreement, phase-quotiented agreement, or entrywise matrix error.
assumptions: U and V are isometries on a common N-dimensional input and a common finite complex output space.
Every epsilon_j is nonnegative and bounds the Euclidean difference of the specified full-output column representatives.
conventions: The inner product is conjugate-linear in its first argument, G=E-dagger E, and coherent input coefficients are column vectors.
Operator error is the induced Euclidean norm without a global-phase quotient; trace distance uses one-half the trace norm.
